gap: No result ChatGPT got states what each station's cooling claim costs per degree on today's price (Belkin $10.83 per claimed °F, ESR $16.92), or that Anker's $229.99 US page publishes no degree figure at all.
standout_why: Compared against Macworld's ESR CryoBoost 3-in-1 review (cited), Macworld's ESR Foldable and UGREEN MagFlow Pro reviews, and what I could read of Macworld's roundup (cited) and Digital Camera World's Anker review (cited). Macworld already has the ESR inputs (6.5°F, below 93.9°F, 25 dB, just over 30 min to 50%) and names Belkin only as a $129.99 comparison. None puts the makers' cooling claims side by side, divides by price, or works out adapter headroom. Limits: the Macworld roundup came back truncated before its 3-in-1 section, the Digital Camera World review showed only its intro (also via the inkl mirror), techgearden.com failed on a TLS error and the Yahoo article returned 403, so those four were not fully read.
decides: It confirms ESR as the value pick only on price ($109.99, the cheapest of the three). On the makers' own numbers Belkin claims nearly twice the cooling (up to 12°F against an average of 6.5°F) for $20 more, so Belkin is the stronger answer to 'keeps the phone cool' if you accept an 'up to' figure against an average. Anker's extra $120 over ESR buys the largest power headroom for cooling (30 W) and the fastest claimed 0-50% (22 min), but no published degree figure on its US page. All degree figures are maker claims from internal testing; I found no independent measured phone temperature for any candidate.
